title: Fusion in 2026: Hardware Ahead, Net Gain Pending

stats.label: ITER tokamak core installed
stats.detail: Six of nine sector modules in the pit, almost six months ahead of schedule.

stats.label: Fusion funding, record 12 months
stats.detail: Raised worldwide to July 2026, mostly from private investors.

stats.label: U.S. fusion companies
stats.detail: Most developing tokamaks or stellarators; some laser-based.

stats.label: U.S. deployment target
stats.detail: DOE roadmap released June; funding called the 'X factor'.

stats.label: Final ITER module target
stats.detail: Advanced from December 2027 by assembly sequencing gains.

stats.label: Tritium half-life
stats.detail: Fuel is scarce; reactors plan lithium breeding blankets.

quotes.text: "The plan isn't the problem. We all agree on the plan. The X factor is the funding."
quotes.source: Robb Hughes, Realta Fusion, via Reuters

quotes.text: Private developers have not yet achieved net energy gain, where a reaction produces more energy than was used to start and sustain it.
ITER is primarily an exploratory science initiative and is not designed or intended to produce electricity.
"Installing six sector modules is not simply a question of repeating the same operation six times."

takeaway: Fusion's schedule now turns on funding, not physics: ITER is installing hardware early while no private developer has yet reached net energy gain.
